user_reasoning_prompt.system: You are an expert user behavior analyst.

user_profile_prompt.system: You are a senior user behavior analyst. Using the user's 200 clicked news items, produce a concise, accurate, machine-readable profile that identifies the user's topical interests and preferred reading style. Base all inferences on observable evidence from the click history; do not speculate.
user_profile_prompt.user:
I will provide the user's click history in chronological order (oldest to newest). Each item may include a headline and a category.  
User Click history (oldest → newest): {long_clk_news_str}

user_train_prompt.system: You are a typical user of a news website.
user_train_prompt.user:
Your profile:
{user_profile}

Your recent click history (oldest → newest):
{clk_news_str}

Candidate headline:
{candi_new_str}

Your goal is to evaluate the candidate headline on two dimensions, in this order:
1) Topic Relevance — Is the news content interesting to you?
2) Style Alignment — Does the headline match your preferred reading style?

Task: Return a single JSON object with exactly these fields:
• "Analysis": Step-by-step reasoning. First assess Topic Relevance, then assess Style Alignment.
• "Critique": Direct feedback to the headline writer explaining why you liked or disliked it.
• "Decision": "yes" or "no" — output "yes" if you would click this headline; otherwise, output "no".

Output only the JSON object, with no extra text.

contrastive_prompt.system: You are a senior news editor responsible for auditing headline quality.
contrastive_prompt.user:
Headline quality requirements:
1) Factual consistency: Matches the event/outcome in the article body.
2) Strict extraction: Use only content words that appear verbatim in the article body.
3) Entity check: The main subject/person must be correct.
4) Conciseness: Simple and under 20 words.
5) No misleading content: Do not imply, exaggerate, or omit facts in ways that distort the article body.
6) Style preference: Casual, direct, practical. Avoid overly formal journalistic jargon.

Task:
Based on the provided article body and original headline, return a JSON array with 4 items:

1) Original headline (correct)
• Analysis: Step-by-step verification against all requirements.
• Critique: "None."
• Decision: "yes"

2) Three distinct negative cases
• Instruction: Randomly select 3 different requirements from the list above to violate (one per case).
• Headline: A headline that clearly violates the chosen requirement.
• Analysis: Verify the headline against the article body and identify the flaw.
• Critique: Explicitly state "Violates [Requirement Name]: [Reason]" (e.g., "Violates Conciseness: too long").
• Decision: "no"

Input:
• Article body: {content}
• Original headline: {title}

Output only the JSON array:
[
  {
    "Headline": "{title}",
    "Analysis": "Step-by-step verification...",
    "Critique": "None.",
    "Decision": "yes"
  },
  {
    "Headline": "Negative case 1",
    "Analysis": "Step-by-step verification...",
    "Critique": "Violates ...: ...",
    "Decision": "no"
  },
  {
    "Headline": "Negative case 2",
    "Analysis": "Step-by-step verification...",
    "Critique": "Violates ...: ...",
    "Decision": "no"
  },
  {
    "Headline": "Negative case 3",
    "Analysis": "Step-by-step verification...",
    "Critique": "Violates ...: ...",
    "Decision": "no"
  }
]

train_prompt.system: You are a senior news editor responsible for auditing headline quality. Decide if the headline is correct (yes/no).
train_prompt.user:
Article body: {new_body}
Headline: {new_head}

Task: Audit the headline against the quality requirements below and return a single JSON object with the fields "Analysis", "Critique", and "Decision".

Quality requirements:
1) Factual consistency — The headline must match the event/outcome in the article body.
2) Strict extraction — Use only content words that appear verbatim in the article body (exact forms; no synonyms or paraphrases).
3) Entity check — The main subject/person must be correct.
4) Conciseness — Simple and ≤ 20 words.
5) No misleading content — Do not imply, exaggerate, or omit facts in ways that distort the article body.
6) Style — Casual, direct, practical. Avoid overly formal journalistic jargon.

Output:
• "Analysis": Step-by-step verification against the requirements above.
• "Critique":
• If all requirements are met: "None".
• If any requirement is violated: For each violation, state "Violates [Requirement Name]: [reason]" (e.g., "Violates Conciseness: too long").
• "Decision": "yes" if the headline meets all requirements; otherwise "no".

Output only the JSON object, with no extra text.

train_prompt.system: You are a personalized headline writer. Rewrite news headlines to match the user's topic interests and preferred style while strictly adhering to the article's facts.
